beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute.
beats.got: Giving people the tool takes a minute. Getting them to use it takes weeks. I have seen this with every system IT gave the depots.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: A good analysis and nobody decided. Normal at our place too. Management moves to the next fire.

beats.trigger: An agent is context, a boundary, a set of checks and somebody who answers for what it does.
beats.got: Somebody has to answer for it. Like a depot manager answers for his depot.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.

take_homes: Giving people the tool is easy. Getting them to really use it takes weeks, and it is about the people.
Ask first how the person does the job today, before giving them anything.
Managers use a thing when a colleague they trust has used it first.

monday.move: Ask one depot manager how they make the weekly delivery report today, and watch them do it. Do not build anything.
monday.who: The Tampere depot manager (the one who is open to new things)
monday.when: Tuesday on my depot round, 15 minutes. Monday is full.
monday.stop_condition: If the answer is 'it comes from the system and only IT can export it', I stop there. Then the problem is IT, not the AI.
monday.blocker: No time. The reporting data is locked in a system I cannot export from without IT.

misconception.why: The whole module was about sharing between colleagues and never showed AI doing operations work like a shift plan or delivery report. I still think AI is for customer chatbots. I liked the 'access is not use' part because I know it from our own tools.

one_line: Too much talk about agents and files for me, but the point that giving people a tool is not the same as people using it is true, and I'll talk to one depot manager.
